question: Can one final selection-specific visual check immediately before the ordinary Right effect reject current B while allowing stable A, unrelated pointer movement, and return to the same living A?
one_primary_change: Add a final A-selection handle predicate immediately before effect input; no production/runtime integration claim.

decision.pass: All 15 valid-A cases final-check true, admit exactly one Right, move A +2 and B 0; all 5 switch-to-B cases final-check false, admit no Right and move neither object; all 20 preserve focus and empty physical input after the decision/effect; independent audit passes.
decision.fail_false_admit: Any switch-to-B case admits the Right effect or moves any object.
decision.fail_false_stop: Any stable, unrelated-pointer, or same-A-return case refuses or fails the exact A-only effect.
decision.harness_fail: Render/source/process/release/integrity failure; stop block without replacing a measured case.

limits: The final check is not atomic with the later effect; a selection change after the check remains possible.
One Inkscape version/layout/action on one container host.
Deliberately authored trajectories; no natural failure-rate claim.
Standalone XTEST harness, not full latest Executor/caller stack and not a speed claim.
